answer: Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 112 answers need 112 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Because the comet index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the haven audit republishes the full set. Reusing one run across aliases collides on the river identifier and voids the later submissions, thus the operator burns for 112 runs and collects one. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
